items.name: Spec Compliance
items.note: C1-C5 implemented exactly per the campaign BRIEF, narrowed by the operator's live decision to convert only #8 (not #7) this pass; no scope creep.

items.name: Error Handling
items.note: collect_external_review_states now catches NotADirectoryError explicitly and returns a structured error row instead of letting it escape; C4 replaces two unguarded raises with is_file() gates.

items.name: Security Basics
items.note: No user input, SQL, HTML rendering, secrets, or auth/permission surface touched — this is filesystem-discovery and test-corpus code only.

items.name: Test Quality
items.note: Every new/renamed test asserts a real outcome (explicit error row's reason field, a skipped directory not raising, candidate_count liveness guards); the sort=True/False revert-and-restore experiment confirmed the C5 seam probes are not vacuous before adding the guard.

items.name: Performance Basics
items.note: No query patterns, no unbounded list endpoints; changes are directory-walk guard logic and a path-separator fix.

items.name: Naming & Structure
items.note: File locations match existing plugin/shared layout. spec_parser.py, drift_parsers.py, and test_data_collector.py exceed 300 lines predating this change. The session's bloat anti-ratchet caught two real ratchets before commit: (1) a C5 nit moving comments into docstrings grew spec_parser.py/drift_parsers.py further -- fixed by reverting to inline comments extended in place, net line delta against origin/main now exactly zero; (2) the mandatory C1 test grew test_data_collector.py past its existing ADR-092 bloat-exception `current` ceiling -- fixed by trimming a redundant docstring, then deliberately bumping `current` (1029->1039) in shipwright_bloat_baseline.json, since ADR-092 already argues this specific file is a deep test module and a legitimate new test is exactly the case that exception exists for.

items.name: Affected Boundaries
items.note: Serialized format changed: integration-tests/requirements_corpus/golden.json. Producer: regen_golden.py (run with --reason, the exact string mandated by the BRIEF's Q1). Consumers: the golden-pinned tests in test_requirements_corpus_registry.py / test_requirements_corpus_found_defects.py / test_requirements_corpus_probe_table.py. Round-trip (regenerate -> full corpus suite reads it -> green) verified directly; no touches_io_boundary risk flag fired (this is a committed test fixture, not a runtime config/state file).
